section_1.title: The Hook: An Impossible Connection
section_1.content: Introduce the counter-intuitive phenomenon: how the collision of two blocks with mass ratios of powers of 100 calculates the digits of pi. Establish the surprise factor.
section_1.example: Imagine two blocks, one massive (mass M) and one tiny (mass m=1), sliding toward each other. The number of total collisions equals the digits of pi.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
section_2.content: Briefly review the conservation of momentum and kinetic energy in perfectly elastic collisions. Introduce the 'V-Space' coordinate system as a geometric representation.
section_2.example: Using a 2D velocity graph: represent the velocity of block A on the x-axis and block B on the y-axis. A collision is a reflection across a line defined by the mass ratio.

section_3.title: Geometric Mapping: From Collisions to Arcs
section_3.content: Explain how the velocity vectors transition from a linear trajectory to an elliptical arc in phase space. The scaling factor of the mass (100^n) creates the specific curvature of a circle.
section_3.example: Visualize the velocity state as a point moving on an ellipse. When the mass ratio is 100^n, the ellipse becomes a circle, and the number of 'bounces' represents the arc length or pi.

section_4.title: Step-by-Step Demonstration: The 1-100 Case
section_4.content: Walk through the visualization: Block A hits Block B, which hits the wall, which hits Block A. Show how the geometry of the collision cycle maps to pi ≈ 3.14.
section_4.example: An animation of a large block (100kg) and a small block (1kg) colliding. Counting the bounces: 3, then 1, then 4—the first three digits of pi emerge mathematically.

section_5.title: Synthesis & Summary
section_5.content: Summarize that this is not a 'magic trick' but a consequence of the conservation laws and the geometric interpretation of elastic collisions. Conclude with the beauty of mathematics in physical systems.
section_5.example: Final slide showing a 'Mechanical Computer' calculating pi, connecting the abstract constant of a circle to the physical momentum of moving objects.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.5
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Observe the 1kg and 100kg blocks.",
            "Wall bounces reflect momentum perfectly.",
            "Total collisions match digits of pi.",
            "We observe exactly 314 total hits.",
            "Geometry bridges mechanics and abstract numbers."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 1-100 Case", lecture_lines)

        block_small = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color="#FFFFFF")
        block_large = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color="#FFFFFF")
        wall = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg", color="#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(block_small, "B2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(block_large, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(block_small), FadeIn(block_large))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(wall, "C5", scale_factor=0.6)
        wall.set_color("#FF4500")
        block_small.set_color("#FF4500")
        block_large.set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(FadeIn(wall), Indicate(block_small), Indicate(wall))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        counter = Text("0", font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(counter, "D2")
        self.play(Write(counter))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        final_count = Text("314", font_size=36, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(final_count, "D4")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(counter, final_count))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#87CEEB")
        wall.set_color("#87CEEB")
        self.play(Indicate(wall))
        self.wait(1)
